January 28, 1976
Length to D. LL. Dlom, ted
Meno to: Herren-H. Oven-
Subject: Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project
GS-110.10
For the past three years I have been sware of the Company's plans for pumped storage development in the valleys of the Blue Ridge escarpment in the vicinity of Lake Jocassee. In as much as possible, I have tried to follow arguments both pro and con concerning this particular development. As the issue has been represented, the reason for this development is to provide storage capacity for a subsequent peak demand. The energy for such storage would be drawn from existing baseline generation facilities during off peak periods. This peaking power capability is the preponderance of the benefit in any cost/benefit analysis. In general, according to the application for license, this facility will operate approximately 7000 hours annually. Approximately 2500 hours of generation will be expected annually. Of course most of this peaking power will be generated during periods in which the weather is at annual temperature extremes; this also being discussed in the application for license. I feel that the causative agents for peak demands are familiar enough not to warrant discussion. If one assumes that this and existing facilities are adequate to meet demand - then the benefit is clear.
Being familiar with the area of this development, I can appreciate the environmental impacts discussed both in the license and in the Draft Environmental Impact Statement. Briefly, a portion of essentially unused, unoccupied land in nearly its natural state will be used and inundated by the reservoir, generation facilities and rights of way. This will be constructed through and into an area of such size and beauty that may render it unique in lands other than parks or National Forests. Wildlife, both flora and fauna, will be displaced or destroyed. Habitat for unique forms will be lost. That same habitat could also support other species that are being restored after depletion due to past impacts by man. An integral part of the fishery of Lake Jocassee will be impacted by the construction of this development.
The justification of such a trade-off is the focus of this letter. The Company has made its predictions of future peak demands. However, as I write this letter it will have been approximately two years since the submission of those predictions. In view of recent changes of factors affecting such a prediction, are these still accurate?
